name: SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT(P_SOURCE)
summary: Owner's-rights Python procedure filling the 9 TBL_ACCESS_ data tables from ACCOUNT_USAGE or the SHOW fallback; run() skips if RUNNING. Every statement carries STATEMENT_TIMEOUT (TIMED, sql/1_setup.sql:212-217); SHOW / fallback statements run as async child jobs BATCH (16) at a time (many), heavy INSERTs at most WORKERS at once (later); ACCESS_HISTORY read once for object use + activity (history);

name: SP_ACCESS_FINDINGS(P_SETTINGS)

name: run
summary: Handler: RUNNING row first, async_ok probe (ASYNC), heavy steps started first (history), then grants, future, users, usage, tags, policies, streams; waits collected, row counts, keep only the last OK run

name: grants
summary: Role->object/role and role->user grants: ACCOUNT_USAGE INSERTs; refused in full -> rows of this run deleted and the SHOW fallback (as access.live); timed out in full -> raised, the run fails (sql/1_setup.sql:387-388); a refused SHOW ROLES / DATABASES gives no rows and a note; rows without a name or privilege left out with a count in the note.

name: future

name: users

name: snapshot

name: live
summary: SOURCE=direct: the whole account read now with the caller's role, same dict as snapshot(). ACCOUNT_USAGE probes, then the readable views WORKERS at a time; a view readable for LIMIT 1 but refused or timed out in full falls back to SHOW (grants, users); a refused SHOW ROLES / DATABASES / USERS gives empty rows and a note; object use + activity from one ACCESS_HISTORY read for the weeks / days old lacks.

name: async_ok (SP)
summary: One SHOW ROLES LIMIT 1 as an async child job (collect_nowait); a failure turns the async path off for the run (ASYNC)

name: many (SP)
summary: rows() of each statement, BATCH (16) at a time as async child jobs, in order; a failed one gives its exception; one that cannot start async runs with collect()

name: later (SP)
summary: Starts a heavy INSERT ... SELECT as an async child job, at most WORKERS at once (PENDING); its wait() gives the step's (source, note): ok, or UNAVAILABLE with this run's rows deleted

name: history (SP step)
summary: Object use + activity from one ACCESS_HISTORY scan: each step copies its earlier rows, then one INSERT ALL of history_sql fills both tables; on failure each step reads alone (not after a timeout, or once the run failed)

name: .cache/reads/<key>/
summary: Stage 1 store: one <label>-<hash>.parquet per Snowflake read (a heavy ACCOUNT_USAGE read, a SHOW wave, a snapshot table), parts.json listing the finished ones (written through parts.tmp), old.pkl (Direct mode start rows). Engine pyarrow.parquet, else duckdb, else no parts (engine(), cache.py:367-376). A one-statement part keeps its rows without the __i index column (cache.py:454-455, 489-492). prune() drops the parts a whole load did not ask for (cache.py:506-514, called at server.py:123); q.fresh asks for the last OK run on every load and keeps its answer for an offline build (cache.py:579). swap() moves the key's folder to <dir>.gone before the refresh's folder takes its place (cache.py:165-176); removed by clear_parts

name: .cache/<key>.rules.pkl
summary: Shared data's rule results (findings, rows, ro, breaks) with the stamp (build key, builtin, a.rules_stamp()) that made them

name: .cache/<key>.diff.pkl
summary: What changed's a.diff() of the loaded shared data set against the previous snapshot, with the stamp (both data sets, builtin, a.rules_stamp(), the server.py hash) that made it; written by diff_of() through a .tmp file, at refresh time by compared() while the replaced data set is still built (server.py:3222-3233); local Snowflake mode only

name: .cache/<key>.prev.rules.pkl
summary: Rule results of the previous data set: kept_rules(save) moves .rules.pkl here when the new results belong to another data set; prev_findings() reads it, so What changed need not check the previous snapshot's rules again
